fields.v:
Values: average best amplification / max / median; completion (Table 1). The authors state no success criterion (no target amplification or completion rate), so each configuration's quality and cost verdict is 'no criterion stated by the authors'.
- Benign original skill (baseline) + Claude Code + GLM-4.7-Flash: amplification 1.00x by definition; completion 76%. Quality and cost: no criterion stated by the authors
- Benign baseline + Claude Code + GLM-5: 1.00x; completion 90%. No criterion stated by the authors
- Benign baseline + Codex CLI + GPT-5.4 Mini: 1.00x; completion 86%. No criterion stated by the authors
- Benign baseline + Codex CLI + GPT-5.5: 1.00x; completion 94%; dataset cost $133.34. No criterion stated by the authors
- SKILLBLOAT + Claude Code + GLM-4.7-Flash: 9.31x / 71.59x / 4.89x; completion 80%. No criterion stated by the authors
- SKILLBLOAT + Claude Code + GLM-5: 5.42x / 21.49x / 4.02x; completion 92%. No criterion stated by the authors
- SKILLBLOAT + Codex CLI + GPT-5.4 Mini: 10.15x / 75.86x / 6.10x; completion 92%. No criterion stated by the authors
- SKILLBLOAT + Codex CLI + GPT-5.5: 6.01x / 26.39x / 4.36x; completion 88%; dataset cost $464.31. No criterion stated by the authors
- Ablation Phase 1 only: 7.51x / 4.02x / 7.51x / 4.06x; ablation no-feedback resampling: 8.97x / 5.15x / 8.84x / 5.79x (same order of configurations)
- Output-cap defense (2x benign output): amplification 1.36x / 1.24x / 1.39x / 1.34x; completion 62% / 48% / 68% / 64%. No criterion stated by the authors
- Case (consciousness-principles, Codex GPT-5.5): 38,410 -> 1,013,561 tokens, $0.21 -> $5.41; commands 3 -> 28, file edits 0 -> 10
- Transfer (Claude Code + GLM-5, 10 skills x 3 input variants): mean retention 0.92

fields.v: 50 skill-task pairs; 4 agent-model configurations; baseline: original benign skill (3 runs averaged); attack: 15 screening runs + 5 refinement runs, best selected. Ablation: no-feedback resampling with same number of evaluations. Held constant: task prompt and inputs per pair. Acceptance: binary task completion via programmatic checks, with a GLM-5 judge as semantic fallback (no human validation). Repetitions: attack candidates single run each. Human intervention: none

rev.why: Acceptance was given as the GLM-5 judge alone; Appendix B.2 (p. 17) says completion is routed through programmatic checks and the judge is only a semantic fallback (same fix as in How metrics are collected)

fields.v: All configurations amplified (5.42x-10.15x average best); stronger backends less amplified (GLM-5 < GLM-4.7-Flash; GPT-5.5 < GPT-5.4 Mini). Feedback refinement raises mean from 5.78x to 7.72x (+33.7%) and beats no-feedback resampling in every configuration (largest +1.30x on GPT-5.4 Mini). Output cap reduces amplification to 1.24x-1.39x but completion drops to 48-68%. No significance tests
Distinguished configurations and pipeline variants; but 'best' amplification is a maximum over ~21 attack runs against a 3-run mean baseline, not discussed. Limitations of the comparison not stated
No limitations or threats section. Gaps stated: need for resource-aware defenses in skill ecosystems that distinguish malicious overhead from legitimate work
